question.problem:
A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below. Find $\text{E}[{e}^{X}].$

| $x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |

current_example.problem:
A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below.  Find $\textrm{E}\big[5e^{1-X}\big].$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.8$ |
current_example.worked_solution:
For a discrete random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\textrm{E}[r(X)] = \sum_{x \in S} r(x) f(x).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=5e^{1-x}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[5{e}^{1-x}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}5{e}^{1-x}\cdot f(x) \\  & =5{e}^{1-1}\cdot 0.2+5{e}^{1-2}\cdot 0.8 \\  & =5{e}^{0}\cdot 0.2+5{e}^{-1}\cdot 0.8 \\  & =5\cdot 0.2+5{e}^{-1}\cdot 0.8 \\  & =1+4{e}^{-1} \\  & =1+\frac{4}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$
